public_rationale: This is a conditional forecast with no deadline: if 'enough' other companies report what Uber reported, the AI bubble pops. Marcus did not say how many companies would be enough, so it cannot be shown that the condition has been met. By late October 2026, the Nasdaq was about 6% below a record set on October 6, and Meta was raising its AI capital spending. No bubble collapse had happened. But with no deadline and an undefined condition, that does not settle the claim.
limitations: The outcome turns on undefined terms ('enough', 'pops').
Market state checked only up to late October 2026.

from_speaker: if enough other companies report the same
our_interpretation: Antecedent: many companies beyond Uber publicly report that AI spending is not producing proportional productivity gains. 'Enough' is not defined.

Consequent: the AI investment bubble 'pops', read plainly as a sharp, lasting collapse in AI-linked valuations and investment (for example a bear market of 20% or more in leading AI stocks, together with clear cuts to AI spending).
criteria.support_condition: Many companies are documented publicly reporting poor AI returns, followed by a sharp, lasting collapse in AI valuations or investment.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Many companies clearly report poor AI returns, yet AI valuations and investment stay high or keep rising for a long time.
